title: Heterogeneous-region degradation simulation and graceful-absorb DR playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an operational DR playbook and scheduled drill harness to validate graceful absorption of traffic when a primary region experiences heterogeneous degradation (partial compute, networking, and degraded KV cache availability). This work focuses on exercising SLO-driven traffic redistribution, adaptive circuit-breaker thresholds, and automated progressive load-shedding on ingress to avoid catastrophic overload on secondary regions. The output will be a runnable runbook, a set of automated validation tests that assert data consistency after prefix/KV cache rehydration, and dashboards/alerts to prove SLO compliance during the drill.
goals: Prove automated traffic absorption into region B under partial primary-region degradation without violating P99 latency SLOs for critical tenant routes.
Validate circuit-breaker hysteresis and tiered load-shedding policies avoid cascading failures during progressive degradation scenarios.
Confirm backup/restore and KV prefix rehydration maintain read-after-write guarantees for active tenants after failback testing.
Produce a documented playbook with runbook steps, rollback criteria, and post-drill checklist for ops and on-call rotations.
out_of_scope: Full cold-region bootstrapping of brand-new hardware (we will assume standby region has baseline capacity and images pre-baked).
Application-level schema migrations or data model changes.
Long-term capacity rebalancing algorithms — we will only exercise short-term absorb + graceful backoff.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook executed in a staged drill without human-in-the-loop intervention for automated rerouting (canary stage requires manual approval).

Critical routes (auth, tokenstore, inference-gateway) maintain <= 2x baseline P50 and <= 1.2x baseline P99 latency during absorption for tenants with SLA tier 'standard' when load-shedding is enabled per policy.
Circuit-breaker tripping and recovery observed in telemetry with no uncontrolled spike in error-rate (>5% sustained) across the platform during stage transitions.
KV prefix rehydration validated: sample of 200 keys across tenants demonstrate read-after-write consistency within 30s after restore steps in the playbook.
Linked dashboards and alerts created; post-drill report generated with timeline, SLO deltas, and recommended policy adjustments.
runbook_steps: Pre-drill: Run automated pre-checks (health of images, standby pool capacity, snapshot integrity). Link to pre-check script: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/dr-precheck
Stage 0 (Canary): Redirect 1% traffic for low-risk tenant subset to standby region via smart routing policy. Verify 5 minute telemetry stability window before proceeding.

Stage 1 (Partial Degradation Simulation): Inject network packet loss (10-30%) into primary-region edge and simulate 20% compute CPU saturation on a subset of serving pods. Activate adaptive CB with aggressive thresholds for non-critical routes.

Stage 2 (Progressive Absorb): Increase routing weight to standby region in 10% increments every 90s for critical routes. Enable tiered load-shedding at ingress for 'best-effort' tenant class when queue depth exceeds X.
Stage 3 (Recovery & Rehydrate): Re-enable primary-region capacity in controlled slices, trigger KV snapshot restore for warmed prefixes, wait for prefix rehydration window and validate key checksums.
Stage 4 (Failback): Gradual traffic shift back to primary with a 5-minute observation window per 10% shift. If P99 regresses beyond threshold, abort and revert to Stage 2 state.
rollback_procedures: Immediate abort: Flip routing config to last-known-good policy stored in ConfigStore and toggle circuit-breaker to conservative mode.
If standby region shows degraded health (node OOMs or disk pressure), trigger emergency throttling on new sessions and enable synchronous write-forwarding to avoid data loss.
Restore traffic to primary only after KV consistency checks pass and P99 latency has stabilized within acceptance bounds.
validation_tests: Telemetry smoke: Assert ingestion of per-route latency and error metrics within 30s of each stage transition.
Data consistency: Run read-after-write probes across sampled prefixes (200 keys) pre- and post-rehydrate; failure tolerance <= 2 mismatches.
Load-shedding effectiveness: Simulate surge of client requests with synthetic load generator; confirm that best-effort tenants are shed according to policy and critical tenants remain within SLOs.

Circuit-breaker replay: Inject repeated transient errors to ensure CB transitions (CLOSED->OPEN->HALF-OPEN->CLOSED) follow configured hysteresis and that recovery attempts do not oversubscribe downstream.
metrics_and_slo_assertions: Critical route P99 <= 1.2x baseline during absorption; P50 <= 2x baseline.
Error rate for critical routes < 1% sustained; overall platform error rate < 5% during stage transitions.
KV rehydration median time < 45s for warmed prefixes; 95th percentile < 120s.
Circuit-breaker open fraction should not exceed 15% for more than 2 minutes for critical paths.
telemetry_checks: Alert on sudden delta in inter-region egress (>30% change in 60s).
Dashboard panels for route-level latencies, backend queue depth, CB state counts, restore throughput (keys/sec).
Tracing: sample traces for critical flows with injected degradation flags to inspect tokenstore and KV paths.
automation_and_artifacts: Drill orchestration job in CI: jobs/drill/hetero-absorb.yaml — will run staged traffic shifts and smoke validations.
Pre-built terraform plan to allocate temporary standby capacity for the drill: infra/terraform/dr-standby-plan.
Validation harness: https://git.internal/redwood/dr/validation-harness (includes probe runners and KV checksum script).
